newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia Sayansk aluminium sees 97 output up 2-3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Russia Sayansk aluminium sees 97 output up 2-3 pct.

text.p: Russia's Sayansk aluminium smelter plans to increase output by two to three percent in 1997, company spokesman Valentin Kornev said on Thursday.
"This year, we plan to increase production in real terms by two to three percent, and in a few years time, to 380,000 tonnes a year," he said in a brief interview, repeating earlier forecasts.
Sayansk produced 327,700 tonnes of primary aluminium in 1996, up from 315,900 tonnes in 1995.
Enriched anode production rose 0.6 percent in 1996 compared to 1995's 230,700 tonnes.
Sayansk, based in southern Siberia, is the third-largest aluminium producer in Russia, which was the world's largest aluminium exporter last year with deliveries of 2.44 million tonnes.
Sayansk accounted for about 11 percent of Russia's total 1997 primary aluminium output of 2.87 million tonnes.
